value.first: At 6 months he's right on time. I'd use iron-first solids with early-and-often allergens, the Health Canada and CPS approach. His iron stores run low around now. Big trials also found that waiting on allergens backfires: early, regular peanut cut peanut allergy by roughly 80%. Start once he sits without support, leans in, and doesn't tongue food back out. If you'd rather skip purees, baby-led weaning follows the same rules.
value.second: Day 1: when he's rested and a bit hungry, sit him fully upright in a high chair. Offer a spoon or two of iron-fortified cereal mixed with milk, pureed beef, or mashed lentils. Days 2-7: iron food twice a day, plus veg and fruit; milk continues as usual. Week 2, peanut: thin half a teaspoon of smooth peanut butter, give a tiny taste, wait 10 minutes, then the rest. Watch him 2 hours. Never a glob, never whole nuts, no honey.
value.third: Then add one new allergen every day or two: cooked egg, yogurt, wheat, tofu, tahini, thinned nut butters, flaked fish. Keep each about twice a week once tolerated, since stopping can undo the protection. Gagging is noisy and normal, and lumpy textures should be in by 9 months. If a food brings hives, a spreading rash or vomiting, stop it and see your provider before offering it again. I'll check in Friday.
